title: Throttled-probe orchestration and token-aware shedding to protect SLOs during regional failover
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: During cross-region failover and large KV-cache warmups we observe rapid readiness/liveness probe flapping that drives aggressive autoscaling and incorrect load-shedding decisions. This causes SLO blips (p95 latency and request error rate) and noisy scale events that destabilize serving pools. Goal: Implement a coordinated, token-aware probe orchestration layer + regional hysteresis to dampen probe noise, apply per-request token budgets for shedding (rather than blunt errors), and add a controlled regional failover plan that preserves SLOs while minimizing overscale/cold-start amplification.
acceptance_criteria: Probe-flap incidents (probe transition count per minute) reduced by >= 70% during simulated failover and KV warmup in chaos test
P95 latency and 99th error rate remain within SLO window during simulated regional failover (end-to-end benchmark against canary workload)
Autoscaler scale-up events during warmup limited to defined budget (<= 2x baseline in first 5 minutes) and no cascading multi-region scale waves
Token-aware shedding implemented: requests above dynamic budget are returned with structured 429 + retry-after and observed to reduce tail latency vs baseline 500 errors
Runbook updated and on-call can trigger manual fallback switch and safe-mode shedding configuration
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — instrumented probe-flap metric (probe_state_changes/min) and token-budget signal in staging. Observed correlated spikes with KV cache misses and cold-start GPU utilization.
2026-03-05: Implemented prototype 'staggered readiness' middleware that introduces per-instance probe offsets and randomized probe jitter; basic test shows 30% reduction in immediate probe fanout.
2026-03-08: Added token-budget header (X-RW-TokenBudget) to internal routing in canary; initial shedding strategy returns structured 429 with retry-after and light tracing.

2026-03-10: Chaos test (region failover + 2x traffic) shows autoscaler flapping persists due to synchronous readiness timeouts; decided to add adaptive probe damping (exponential backoff of probe aggressiveness after first N failures).

2026-03-12: Design review with SRE and product — approved phased rollout: (1) probe jitter + token-budget in canary; (2) adaptive damping + regional hysteresis; (3) circuit-breaker tuning and runbook updates. Owner assignment done.

2026-03-14: PR #4821 opened for staggered readiness offsets and token-budget header. Integration tests failing on Canary due to older SDK ignoring X-RW-TokenBudget header; mitigation path: backwards-compatible default budgeting policy.
reviews: 2026-03-11 - SRE review by Gabriel Santos: requested metrics for autoscale churn (scale events/min) and suggested adding a per-region smoothing window to prevent traffic oscillation.
2026-03-12 - Product review by Maya Patel: emphasized customer-facing error shape and required structured 429 payload with guidance for SDK retries and observability hooks.
2026-03-13 - Security review by Laila O'Connor: no secrets exposure, flagged need to document token-budget propagation for private deployments (VPC) — added to release notes checklist.
2026-03-14 - Peer review by Yun Park: code quality OK, requested more unit tests around backoff math and added a test plan for cold-start GPU behavior.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Favor token-aware shedding (graceful 429) over blind circuit-breaker 500s to reduce client-side retry storms. Tradeoff: some clients will need SDK updates to benefit fully; mitigation: default server-side budget behavior remains conservative for older clients.

Decision: Implement probe offsetting + adaptive backoff rather than increasing probe timeouts globally. Tradeoff: increased probe complexity per-instance; benefit: localizes delay and retains faster detection for truly dead instances.

Decision: Regional hysteresis window is set to 180s by default (configurable per deployment). Tradeoff: slower failover recovery vs fewer oscillations—product accepts slightly longer failover time to preserve SLOs under load.

Tradeoff: Cache warmup mitigation via transient traffic shaping (front-door throttling) vs pre-warming GPUs — chosen to implement transient shaping first (faster to deploy), with pre-warm as follow-up if shaping insufficient.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy staggered readiness offsets + X-RW-TokenBudget header to 2% of traffic in region-us-east-1. Monitor probe_state_changes/min, autoscale events/min, p95 latency.
Phase 1 (regional): enable adaptive probe damping and token-aware shedding in one secondary region; keep default client budget for older SDKs.
Phase 2 (global): enable regional hysteresis and automatic failover policy with gradual traffic migration (10% steps, 2m wait) and abort criteria based on SLO delta.
Fallback: runbook 'slo-stability-fallback' to perform manual traffic shift and enable 'safe-mode' shedding config if p99 errors exceed threshold for 3 consecutive windows.
metrics_to_watch: request retry rate (client-side) and observed retry-after adherence
